# package uacp

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/uacp"
```

Package uacp provides encoding/decoding and automated connection handling for the OPC UA Connection Protocol.

To establish the connection as a client, call the Dial() function.

To wait for the client to connect to, call Listen() method, and to establish connection with the Accept() method.

For a reverse connection (Part 6 §7.1.3), in which the server opens the TCP connection and announces itself with a ReverseHello message, the server uses ReverseDialer and Conn.AcceptHello and the client uses ListenReverse and Dialer.AcceptReverse.

Once you have a connection you can call Read() to receive full UACP messages including the header.

In uacp, \*Conn also implements Local/RemoteEndpoint() methods which returns EndpointURL of client or server.

The data on top of UACP connection is passed as it is as long as the connection is established. In other words, uacp never cares the data even if it seems invalid. Users of this package should check the data to make sure it is what they want or not.

```go
const (
	// SchemeWebSocket is the URL scheme of WebSocket endpoints.
	SchemeWebSocket = "opc.wss"

	// WebSocketSubprotocol is the WebSocket sub-protocol that carries UACP
	// (Part 6 §7.5.2).
	WebSocketSubprotocol = "opcua+uacp"

	// WebSocketJSONSubprotocol is the WebSocket sub-protocol that carries
	// service messages in the JSON encoding (Part 6 §7.5.2).
	WebSocketJSONSubprotocol = "opcua+uajson"

	// defaultWebSocketPort is the port of an opc.wss URL without one: the
	// HTTPS port, since the connection starts as an HTTPS request.

)
```

The WebSocket transport of the OPC UA Connection Protocol (Part 6 §7.5): the UACP messages and the secure conversation on top of them travel in binary WebSocket frames over TLS, one MessageChunk per frame. The HEL/ACK handshake runs after the WebSocket opening handshake, as on TCP.

The sub-protocol opcua+uajson (transport profile wss-uajson) carries no UACP: each WebSocket message is one service request or response in the JSON encoding (Part 6 §7.5.2, §5.4.9), there is neither a HEL/ACK nor a secure conversation, and TLS alone protects the messages. Such connections are MessageConns.

## Variables

```go
var (
	// DefaultClientACK is the ACK handshake message sent to the server
	// for client connections.
	DefaultClientACK = &Acknowledge{
		ReceiveBufSize: DefaultReceiveBufSize,
		SendBufSize:    DefaultSendBufSize,
		MaxChunkCount:  0, // the server's limit, or DefaultMaxChunkCount
		MaxMessageSize: 0, // the server's limit, or DefaultMaxMessageSize
	}

	// DefaultServerACK is the ACK handshake message sent to the client
	// for server connections.
	DefaultServerACK = &Acknowledge{
		ReceiveBufSize: DefaultReceiveBufSize,
		SendBufSize:    DefaultSendBufSize,
		MaxChunkCount:  DefaultMaxChunkCount,
		MaxMessageSize: DefaultMaxMessageSize,
	}
)
```

## Functions

### func DialTCP

```go
func DialTCP(ctx context.Context, endpoint string) (net.Conn, error)
```

DialTCP establishes a TCP connection to the OPC UA endpoint address only. It parses the endpoint URL (e.g. opc.tcp://host:4840/path) and opens a TCP connection, leaving hostname resolution to net.Dialer. No OPC UA HEL/ACK or secure channel is performed. The caller must close the returned connection. Use this for TCP reachability checks (e.g. "ping" or connection diagnostics) without creating a session or secure channel.

### func DialTCPWithTimeout

```go
func DialTCPWithTimeout(ctx context.Context, endpoint string, timeout time.Duration) (net.Conn, error)
```

DialTCPWithTimeout is like DialTCP but uses the given dial timeout. A zero timeout means no limit (beyond any deadline on ctx).

### func IsWebSocketEndpoint

```go
func IsWebSocketEndpoint(endpoint string) bool
```

IsWebSocketEndpoint reports whether endpoint is an opc.wss URL.

### func ParseEndpoint

```go
func ParseEndpoint(endpoint string) (network string, u *url.URL, err error)
```

ParseEndpoint parses and validates an OPC UA endpoint URL without performing DNS resolution. The returned URL has its Host field normalized to host:port form. Hostname resolution is deferred to net.Dialer or net.Listen at connection time so the standard library can apply its own address selection, including IPv4/IPv6 fallback behavior.

Expected format: "opc.tcp://\<host\[:port]>/path"

### func ParseWebSocketEndpoint

```go
func ParseWebSocketEndpoint(endpoint string) (*url.URL, error)
```

ParseWebSocketEndpoint parses and validates an opc.wss endpoint URL like ParseEndpoint does for opc.tcp. The Host of the returned URL is in host:port form; the port defaults to 443.

#### func (Conn) AcceptHello

```go
func (c *Conn) AcceptHello(ctx context.Context, endpoint string) (err error)
```

AcceptHello performs the server side of the HEL/ACK exchange on a connection: it waits for the Hello message of the client, checks that it names endpoint, and answers with Acknowledge.

It is meant for reverse connections (see ReverseDialer), where the Hello message arrives whenever the client decides to use the connection, which can be long after it was opened. AcceptHello therefore waits until ctx is done.

```go
	Dialer *net.Dialer
```

#### func (Dialer) AcceptReverse

```go
func (d *Dialer) AcceptReverse(ctx context.Context, l *ReverseListener, endpoint string, match func(*ReverseHello) error) (*Conn, *ReverseHello, error)
```

AcceptReverse is the reverse-connect counterpart of Dial: instead of connecting to the server it waits for the server to connect to l and to announce itself with a ReverseHello message that satisfies match (see ReverseListener.Accept), and then performs the HEL/ACK handshake.

The Hello message names the EndpointUrl of the ReverseHello message, as Part 6 §7.1.3 requires; endpoint is used if the server did not send one. The dial timeout bounds the waiting and the handshake together. A zero timeout waits until ctx is done.

#### func (Dialer) AcceptReverseSince

```go
func (d *Dialer) AcceptReverseSince(ctx context.Context, l *ReverseListener, endpoint string, match func(*ReverseHello) error, rejected uint64) (*Conn, *ReverseHello, error)
```

AcceptReverseSince is AcceptReverse for a caller that started waiting before it called it; rejected is the listener's Rejected count at that moment (see ReverseListener.AcceptSince).

#### func (Dialer) Dial

```go
func (d *Dialer) Dial(ctx context.Context, endpoint string) (*Conn, error)
```

Dial connects to endpoint and performs the HEL/ACK handshake. An opc.tcp endpoint is reached over TCP, an opc.wss endpoint over a TLS secured WebSocket with the sub-protocol opcua+uacp (Part 6 §7.5).

#### func (Dialer) DialWebSocketJSON

```go
func (d *Dialer) DialWebSocketJSON(ctx context.Context, endpoint string) (MessageConn, error)
```

DialWebSocketJSON opens a TLS secured WebSocket with the sub-protocol opcua+uajson to an opc.wss endpoint (Part 6 §7.5.2), with the TLS configuration and the dial timeout of d, which covers TLS and the WebSocket upgrade. There is no HEL/ACK on such a connection.

### type Listener

```go
type Listener struct {

	// The TCP accept loop and the HEL/ACK handshakes run in the background
	// so that a peer which connects but does not (or only slowly) send its
	// HEL cannot keep other peers from being accepted.

	// connections in handshake

	// upgrade turns an accepted TCP connection into the connection UACP
	// runs on, within the handshake deadline: TLS and the WebSocket opening
	// handshake for opc.wss. Nil for opc.tcp.

	// jsonHandler serves the WebSocket connections with the sub-protocol
	// opcua+uajson (ServeWebSocketJSON).

}
```

Listener is a OPC UA Connection Protocol network listener.

#### func Listen

```go
func Listen(ctx context.Context, endpoint string, ack *Acknowledge) (*Listener, error)
```

Listen acts like net.Listen for OPC UA Connection Protocol networks.

Currently the endpoint can only be specified in "opc.tcp://\<addr\[:port]>/path" format.

If the IP field of laddr is nil or an unspecified IP address, Listen listens on all available unicast and anycast IP addresses of the local system. If the Port field of laddr is 0, a port number is automatically chosen.

#### func ListenWebSocket

```go
func ListenWebSocket(ctx context.Context, endpoint string, tlsConfig *tls.Config, ack *Acknowledge) (*Listener, error)
```

ListenWebSocket listens for OPC UA WebSocket connections (Part 6 §7.5) on the host and port of an opc.wss endpoint URL. Each accepted connection is secured with TLS using tlsConfig, which must hold the server's TLS certificate (it may differ from the application instance certificate, Part 6 §7.5.3), upgraded to a WebSocket with the sub-protocol opcua+uacp and then goes through the HEL/ACK handshake. Accept returns connections that completed all three. TLS 1.2 is the minimum version; set ClientAuth and ClientCAs in tlsConfig to require client TLS certificates. With ServeWebSocketJSON the listener also accepts the sub-protocol opcua+uajson.

#### func (Listener) Accept

```go
func (l *Listener) Accept(ctx context.Context) (*Conn, error)
```

Accept returns the next connection that completed the HEL/ACK handshake.

TCP connections are accepted and handshaken in the background, each with a deadline, so a slow or silent peer does not delay other connections. A failed handshake is reported as an error; the caller should keep calling Accept. Accept returns ctx.Err() when ctx is done and a \*net.OpError wrapping net.ErrClosed once the listener is closed.


Addr returns the listener's network address.


#### func (Listener) ServeWebSocketJSON

```go
func (l *Listener) ServeWebSocketJSON(h func(MessageConn))
```

ServeWebSocketJSON makes a WebSocket listener accept the sub-protocol opcua+uajson next to opcua+uacp (Part 6 §7.5.2): a connection that selects it skips the HEL/ACK handshake and is handed to h in a goroutine of its own instead of being returned by Accept. h owns the connection and closes it. Call it before the first Accept; it has no effect on an opc.tcp listener.

### type MessageConn

```go
type MessageConn interface {
	// ReadMessage reads the next message. A message larger than maxSize
	// bytes ends the connection with WebSocket status 1009 (Part 6 §7.5.2).
	// It must not be called from two goroutines at once.
	ReadMessage(maxSize int64) ([]byte, error)
	// WriteMessage sends p as one text message. It may be called
	// concurrently.
	WriteMessage(p []byte) error
	SetReadDeadline(t time.Time) error
	SetWriteDeadline(t time.Time) error
	RemoteAddr() net.Addr
	Close() error
}
```

MessageConn is a WebSocket connection with the sub-protocol opcua+uajson, which carries whole messages instead of a byte stream.

### type ReverseListener

```go
type ReverseListener struct {

	// rejected counts the connections refused by the filter and lastReject
	// is the reason of the latest refusal.

}
```

ReverseListener accepts reverse connections: TCP connections opened by OPC UA servers that announce themselves with a ReverseHello message.

One listener can serve any number of clients and servers. A connection that no client is waiting for is kept (a server keeps one idle connection open for exactly that purpose, see Part 6 §7.1.3) until a client asks for it with Accept, the server closes it, or it is displaced by a newer connection of the same server.

Nothing a server says in its ReverseHello message is authenticated. The message only selects the client the connection is handed to; the server proves its identity in the secure channel that is opened afterwards.

#### func ListenReverse

```go
func ListenReverse(ctx context.Context, addr string, cfg *ReverseListenerConfig) (*ReverseListener, error)
```

ListenReverse opens a listener for reverse connections on addr, which is either a "host:port" address or an "opc.tcp://host:port" URL. An empty or unspecified host listens on all addresses, port 0 picks a free port. cfg may be nil.

#### func NewReverseListener

```go
func NewReverseListener(l net.Listener, cfg *ReverseListenerConfig) *ReverseListener
```

NewReverseListener returns a ReverseListener that accepts the connections of l, which must be a TCP listener. The ReverseListener owns l from now on and closes it when it is closed. cfg may be nil.

#### func (ReverseListener) Accept

```go
func (l *ReverseListener) Accept(ctx context.Context, match func(*ReverseHello) error) (*net.TCPConn, *ReverseHello, error)
```

Accept returns a reverse connection whose ReverseHello message satisfies match, together with that message. It prefers the most recent pending connection and otherwise waits for a server to connect until ctx is done. A nil match accepts any server.

The returned connection is a plain TCP connection on which nothing but the ReverseHello message was exchanged. Most callers want Dialer.AcceptReverse instead, which also performs the HEL/ACK handshake.

match must not block and must not call methods of the listener.

#### func (ReverseListener) AcceptSince

```go
func (l *ReverseListener) AcceptSince(ctx context.Context, match func(*ReverseHello) error, rejected uint64) (*net.TCPConn, *ReverseHello, error)
```

AcceptSince is Accept for a caller that started waiting before it called it: rejected is the value of Rejected when the caller began to wait. If ctx ends the waiting and the filter refused a server since then, the error names the reason, so that a refusal that happened while the caller was still setting up (opening the listener, a failed handshake on an earlier connection) is not lost.


Addr returns the listener's network address.

#### func (ReverseListener) Close

```go
func (l *ReverseListener) Close() error
```

Close closes the listener together with all connections that have not been handed to a client, and waits for the goroutines of the listener to stop. Connections returned by Accept are not affected.

### type ReverseListenerConfig

```go
type ReverseListenerConfig struct {
	// Filter is called with every ReverseHello message that arrives. A
	// connection for which it returns an error is refused: it is answered
	// with an Error message and closed. Use it to admit only the servers
	// that are expected to connect. If nil, every server is admitted.
	//
	// Filter is called from the goroutines of the listener and must not
	// block.
	Filter func(*ReverseHello) error

	// HelloTimeout is how long an accepted connection may take to deliver
	// its ReverseHello message. Defaults to DefaultReverseHelloTimeout.
	HelloTimeout time.Duration

	// MaxHandshakes is the number of accepted connections that may be
	// waiting for their ReverseHello message at the same time. Connections
	// beyond the limit are closed at once. Defaults to
	// DefaultMaxReverseHandshakes.
	MaxHandshakes int

	// MaxPending is the number of announced connections that are kept for a
	// client that has not asked for them yet. When the limit is reached the
	// oldest pending connection is closed. Defaults to
	// DefaultMaxPendingReverse.
	MaxPending int

	// Logger is the logger for connection-level messages.
	// If nil, logging is disabled.
	Logger *slog.Logger
}
```

ReverseListenerConfig configures a ReverseListener. The zero value is a usable configuration.
